newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS HAS SLIGHT TEAR OF KNEE LIGAMENT FROM FALL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS HAS SLIGHT TEAR OF KNEE LIGAMENT FROM FALL.

text.p: World number one Martina Hingis suffered a slight tear of a knee ligament in a horse riding accident on Monday and will miss at least two tournaments, the WTA Tour announced Wednesday.
The 16-year-old Hingis, youngest player ever to hold the top ranking, has withdrawn from the Hamburg event due to begin next Monday and will also miss the Italian Open in Rome the following week.
The Swiss sensation hopes to return to action for the German Open in Berlin the week of May 12.
"I am very disappointed that I will have to miss these next two weeks," Hingis said from her home in Trubbach, Switzerland, according to the WTA Tour statement.
"I was feeling great and was looking forward to returning to the Tour. However, I am also very grateful that there was no major damage to my knee."
Hingis injured her left knee in a fall from a horse near her home on Monday.

She continued riding after her fall but Tuesday morning awoke with some discomfort and swelling and went to a sports medicine specialist at a private clinic in Schrunz, Austria, the tour statement said.
An arthroscopy was performed on her knee, revealing a slight tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. Hingis plans to begin rehabilitating her knee Monday, April 28.
Hingis, according to the tour's statement, added that she fully expects to continue horseback riding as soon as possible.

A keen horsewoman, Hingis escaped injury earlier this year when she landed on soft grass after falling from a horse on the eve of her quarter-final match in the Australian Open. She went on to win the tournament.
